# Cancellation of catalysts whose radical is generated by central nilpotents

With the notation and feasible forward pole caps of [Exact pole-cap cancellation and linear amplification](AmplificationAndCancellation.md), the cancellation in part 2 holds for every nonzero finite-dimensional \(k\)-algebra \(B\) for which \(B/NB\) is semisimple, where \(N\) is the nilradical of \(Z(B)\). This includes all semisimple algebras, even with inseparable centers, and all finite-dimensional commutative algebras and matrix algebras over them. The proof preserves all three caps separately. The conclusion about minimum order of a polynomial presentation therefore holds on this larger class.

Take a witness over \(K=k((t))\) for the algebras \(A_\pm=(A_m^\pm)^{\otimes r}\) tensored with \(B\). Use the normalization and the maps (1) of the power proof, with \(R=k[[t]]\). Since \(Z(A_\pm)=k\), the centers of the source and special endpoints equal \(Z(B)\). In fact, expanding in a basis of \(B\), commuting with \(A_\pm\otimes 1\) forces an element into \(1\otimes B\), and commuting with \(1\otimes B\) then forces it into \(1\otimes Z(B)\). Center ranks agree in the two fibers, so the commutator-kernel unit-minor argument gives base change for the integral center. Lift the local factor idempotents of the special center by the same idempotent iteration. There are equally many local factors in the generic and special centers. Thus \(H\) matches them bijectively, exactly as for the split center argument. The integral algebra splits into the lifted factors, and (1) restricts with the same caps.

In a matched factor write \(C,C'\) for the source and special local centers and \(L,L'\) for their residue fields. Use \(H^{-1}\) to identify the generic center with \(C((t))\). The composite from the integral center to its generic residue \(L((t))\) lands in \(L[[t]]\): each element is integral over \(R\) by finite freeness, and a Laurent series of negative valuation cannot satisfy a monic equation over \(R\), since its leading monic term has uniquely least valuation. Reduction gives a unital map \(C'\to L\). It kills the nilradical and induces a field embedding \(L'\to L\), so \([L':k]\le[L:k]\). The source and special lists of local factors come from the same \(Z(B)\), giving equality of the sums of these dimensions. Consequently each embedding is an isomorphism. The integral center map onto \(L[[t]]\) is now surjective by Nakayama's lemma. Its kernel is a free direct summand with generic and special fibers equal to the respective nilradicals. Take the product of these kernels over the matched factors to obtain a central ideal in the integral law.

Multiply this ideal by the integral algebra. This image of an \(R\)-linear multiplication map is a free direct summand by the unit-minor argument, since the two fiber dimensions are both \(\dim_k A_\pm\cdot\dim_k(NB)\). On both sides of (1) the multiplication-by-unit maps preserve the corresponding ideals, and \(H\) transports them. Consequently all three maps in (1) descend to the source and target quotients. Their cap bounds remain valid, since an integral adapted basis displays each induced map as a block of the original matrix. This produces the same-cap comparison with the semisimple catalyst \(B/NB\).

It remains to cancel an arbitrary semisimple catalyst \(D\). Apply the same normalization and center argument with \(D\) in place of \(B\). Now each local center is already a field, so in each matched factor the integral center map to \(L[[t]]\) is an isomorphism: it surjects and its kernel is free with rank zero. The normalized integral algebra in that factor is a finite torsion-free module over \(L[[t]]\), hence is free. Its source lattice is also free over \(L[[t]]\). In the identification of scalar actions furnished by \(H\), all three maps (1) are \(L((t))\)-linear. The \(R\)-based cap condition is exactly \(t^{p_i}F_i(\text{input lattice})\subseteq\text{output lattice}\), so it gives the same caps in \(L[[t]]\)-bases. The source and special simple factors of \(D\) are central simple over the common \(L\) using the residue identification; their matrix degrees agree by freeness and \(\dim A_+=\dim A_-\). Choose a common splitting field for the two central simple factors and extend coefficients, keeping \(t\) as uniformizer. The two endpoints are now the same-size matrix amplifications of \(A_+,A_-\). Sections 1–2 of the power proof extract integer weights with all three caps and construct a monomial witness over \(k\) itself. Conversely, tensor any unamplified witness with the three identity maps on \(B\). [Central simple algebras and splitting fields](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074X)
